chunks: And that which was narrated: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Isma'il from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about sa'uw (snuff) for the muhrim (one in ihram), and it contains perfume, so he said, 'There is no harm.' It is to be understood as applying in the state of necessity, not in the state of choice.

key_terms.السَّعُوط: Snuff (powdered herbs or spices inhaled through the nose)
key_terms.لِلْمُحْرِم: For the one in ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a person in ihram to use snuff containing perfume?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permitting sa'uw (snuff) with perfume for the muhrim, a ruling scholars interpret as being specific to cases of necessity (darurah) rather than voluntary use. This distinction highlights the principle that prohibitions in ihram are lifted when required for health or relief, distinguishing between essential use and mere preference.
